crossRefs.note: How long will you sleep, sluggard? When will you arise out of your sleep?
He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
He who tills his land shall have plenty of bread, but he who chases fantasies is void of understanding.
The soul of the sluggard desires, and has nothing, but the desire of the diligent shall be fully satisfied.
Slothfulness casts into a deep sleep. The idle soul shall suffer hunger.
I went by the field of the sluggard, by the vineyard of the man void of understanding:
not lagging in diligence; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord;
For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: “If anyone is not willing to work, don’t let him eat.”
So the ship master came to him, and said to him, “What do you mean, sleeper? Arise, call on your God! Maybe your God…
Do this, knowing the time, that it is already time for you to awaken out of sleep, for salvation is now nearer to us…
Wake up righteously, and don’t sin, for some have no knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
Therefore he says, “Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ will shine on you.”

translations.web: Don’t love sleep, lest you come to poverty. Open your eyes, and you shall be satisfied with bread.
translations.bsb: Do not love sleep, or you will grow poor; open your eyes, and you will have plenty of food.
translations.kjv: Love not sleep, lest thou come to poverty; open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
translations.asv: Love not sleep, let thou come to poverty; Open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
